Description

RAS proteins signal from more than one membrane. Live probes showed that endogenous RAS is activated by mitogens on the Golgi apparatus, and that HRAS and NRAS engage RAF1 there, so RAS on different membranes reaches different pathways [1]. On the Golgi the exchange factor is RASGRP1. When Src activates phospholipase Cγ1, RASGRP1 moves to the Golgi and activates RAS there. The same second messenger, Ca2+, switches RAS off at the plasma membrane through the GTPase-activating protein CAPRI (RASA4) [2]. Which membranes a RAS isoform visits depends on its C-terminal anchor. HRAS and NRAS are palmitoylated, shown on the map as the mark Pa. A constant cycle removes and adds back the palmitate: without it RAS spreads to all membranes, palmitoylation traps it on the Golgi, and the secretory pathway returns it to the plasma membrane [3, 4]. The thioesterase APT1 removes the palmitate, and DHHC9 with GCP16 adds it on the Golgi [5, 6]. KRAS4B carries a polybasic stretch instead, which sends it straight to the plasma membrane [4, 7]. Where RAS signals from decides what ERK does. ERK activated by RAS in lipid rafts phosphorylates cPLA2 through KSR1 and the EGF receptor through IQGAP1, ERK activated from the endoplasmic reticulum reaches cPLA2 through Sef, and RAS in the disordered membrane activates RSK1 [8]. In the same study RAS held at the Golgi activated ERK only weakly, so how much the Golgi pool contributes depends on the cell and the readout [8]. The cascade switches on at a low threshold at the plasma membrane and at a high one in the cytosol [9]. HRAS signals most strongly from the plasma membrane, but from the endoplasmic reticulum it regulates the most genes [10].
